bib.title: L-Eval: Instituting Standardized Evaluation for Long Context Language Models

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "L-Eval: Instituting Standardized Evaluation for Long Context Language Models", Chenxin An, Shansan Gong, Ming Zhong, Xingjian Zhao, Mukai Li, Jun Zhang, Lingpeng Kong, Xipeng Qiu. Venue as printed: "preprint", arXiv:2307.11088v3 [cs.CL], 4 Oct 2023. Affiliations as printed (not mapped per author in the extraction): Fudan University, The University of Hong Kong, University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, Shanghai AI Lab.

COVERAGE: 26 of 26 pages, all ~90.9k extracted chars, including appendices A and B; references skimmed. Figures were read by caption only, so bar values in Figure 2 beyond those stated in prose are not reported.

CLAIMS
- claim: Benchmark size.
  number: 20 sub-tasks, 508 documents, over 2,000 pairs, 3k-200k tokens
  setup: Llama2 tokenizer; per-task average length 3,907 to 62,335 tokens; maximum 210,541 (NarrativeQA)
  quote: "20 sub-tasks, 508 long documents, and over 2,000 human-labeled query-response pairs ... input length (3k ∼200k tokens)"
  where: p1; Table 1, p5
- claim: Provenance split is from-scratch, re-annotated, and manually cleaned.
  number: 4 / 4 / 12
  setup: from scratch = Coursera, SFiction, CodeU, LongFQA
  quote: "4 sub-tasks are annotated from scratch (§3.1), 4 sub-tasks are re-annotated from the public datasets (§3.2), and the remaining 12 sub-tasks are manually cleaned"
  where: p1
- claim: Errors in existing datasets were found by having Claude-100k answer each question from the document, with humans re-annotating or removing mismatches.
  number: none (no counts of removed or fixed items are given)
  setup: all reused sets
  quote: "If Claude produces an answer greatly mismatching the ground truth or states that we cannot deduce the answer from the context, we will either perform re-annotation or simply remove them."
  where: p4
  Examples of faults found: NarrativeQA questions whose main character "does not even appear in the input document" (p24); Qasper "identical questions yielded contradictory answers" (p24).
- claim: Closed-ended vs open-ended split is 7 vs 13 tasks.
  number: 7 closed (exact-match accuracy), 13 open
  setup: Table 1 rows; my sums of its columns give 1,047 closed and 1,150 open instructions (2,197 total) and 508 documents
  quote: none for the sums (they are mine); the rows are in Table 1
  where: p5
- claim: The length instruction raises metric-human agreement.
  number: Kendall tau 0.5 to 0.8 for ROUGE-L; 1 for the GPT-4 judge
  setup: system-level ranking of 7 models, 85-question subset, 3 annotators (PhD students), 1-5 scale, greedy decoding
  quote: "τ has been improved from 0.5 to 0.8 for ROUGE-L and τ of GPT-4 evaluator has even reached to 1"
  where: p6
- claim: Without the length instruction, automatic metrics other than GPT-4 do not track humans.
  number: none
  setup: same as above
  quote: "all these automatic metrics (except GPT-4) fail to correlate to human judgment"
  where: p6
- claim: N-gram scores swing with output length.
  number: Claude-100k NQ F-1 9.84 to 57.76 with the length instruction (excess length ΔL 135 to 1)
  setup: NQ subset, Table 2
  quote: "Claude-100k 15.43 45.65 165 14.04 58.77 183 9.84 56.19 135" / "+ Length Instruction ... 57.76 51.00 1"
  where: p7
- claim: GPT-4-32k leads closed-ended tasks.
  number: average 73.11 vs Claude 65.97 vs Turbo-16k 60.73; best open-source (Vicuna1.5-13b-16k) 43.46
  setup: 6 tasks in Table 3 (TopicRet is reported separately)
  quote: "GPT-4-32k ✗ 32k 75.58 96.00 82.17 84.38 25.55 74.99 73.11"
  where: p8
- claim: Claude-100k leads open-ended tasks.
  number: win-rate vs Turbo-16k 60.94% (GPT-4-32k 54.16%; best open-source Llama2-13b-chat 42.44%)
  setup: GPT-4 judge, 96-question subset, 96×2 rounds with order swapped
  quote: "Claude1.3-100k ✗ 100k 96 42 60.94"
  where: p9
- claim: Fine-tuning for longer context helped closed-ended tasks but not open-ended ones.
  number: 34% win-rate, 8 points lower than its short version
  setup: Vicuna1.5-13b-16k vs Llama2-13b-chat, GPT-4 judge
  quote: "Vicuna1.5-13b-16k only wins Turbo-16k by 34%, 8 points lower than its short version Llama2-13b"
  where: p8
- claim: Retrieval with a 4k model trails full context.
  number: 49.73 (AdaEmb) and 49.65 (BM25) vs 60.73 closed-ended average
  setup: top 4 chunks of 1k; GSM drops to 23.00
  quote: "AdaEmb-Turbo-4k-0613 ✓ 4k 61.77 23.00 58.91 76.95 6.66 71.09 49.73"
  where: p8
- claim: Judging everything with GPT-4 was treated as too costly.
  number: about $100 for 4 datasets; about $5 for the 96-question subset
  quote: "Testing the 4 datasets in Table 2 needs about $100!"
  where: p6 footnotes

LIMITS
- No Pearson correlation appears anywhere; only Kendall tau, and only two values are stated in prose.
- Correlation is over 7 systems, not items. No inter-annotator agreement is reported, and the annotators research the same topic.
- The length instruction gives the model the reference's word count, which leaks answer granularity (unstated). It also changes outputs, not only scoring: Claude's human average goes 3.08 to 4.04 (Table 5, p15).
- Claude-100k was both the data filter and an evaluated model (unstated bias risk). Errors Claude agrees with go undetected.
- The LLM judge never sees the document: "evaluation results mainly depend on the reference answer" (p5).
- Authors concede "almost all metrics, including ... the GPT-4 evaluator, exhibit bias" (p15).
- Small subsets (85 and 96 questions); models are 2023 vintage.

BUILDS ON: Zheng et al., 2023 (LLM-as-judge, MT-Bench); Li et al., 2023c (AlpacaEval); Li et al., 2023a (LongChat topic retrieval); Zhang et al., 2023 (CAB); Shaham et al., 2022/2023 (SCROLLS, ZeroScrolls); Lin, 2004 (ROUGE).

CODE: Judge prompt addition (p5): "Additional details or information that are not mentioned in the reference answer cannot be considered as advantages and do not let them sway your judgment." Length-instruction form (p6): "We need a 50-word summary".

FIGURES: Figure 2, p6, "Kendall-Tau correlation coefficient of different automatic metrics with the average human score." It shows each metric with and without the length instruction in one chart.

PROBLEMS
- No embedded instructions aimed at the reader.
- Internal inconsistencies in the paper:
  - "4 sub-tasks" re-annotated (p1) vs "We re-annotate 5 publicly available datasets" (p3), so 4+5+12 = 21, not 20.
  - LongFQA has 52 instructions in Table 1 vs "54 questions" (p23).
  - QuALITY has 15 documents in Table 1 vs "20 long stories" (p20).
  - Multi-News has 11 in Table 1 vs "select 10 articles" (p26).
  - Table 4 prints Turbo-16k tokens as "4k".
  - Figure 3 says six models where the text says seven.
- Table 1's † and * markers are not defined in the caption.
